name: Vienna Game
description: 2.Nc3 and an early f4: a King's Gambit idea with better timing.

lines.name: 3…d5

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: f4 is the Vienna Gambit: it attacks e5 and opens the f-file.
notes.6: fxe5 gains space and pushes the f6 knight away.
notes.12: Bd3 challenges the strong e4 knight.

lines.summary: After 3…d5, take on e5, develop with Nf3, d4 and Bd3, and attack the e4 knight.

lines.name: 7…f5

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: f4 is the Vienna Gambit: it attacks e5 and opens the f-file.
notes.6: fxe5 gains space and pushes the f6 knight away.
notes.12: Bd3 challenges the strong e4 knight.
notes.14: exf6 takes en passant, opening the f-file for White's rook.
notes.16: O-O puts the rook on the open f-file, aimed at f7.

lines.summary: If Black props up the knight with …f5, take en passant and castle onto the open f-file.

lines.name: 5…Bg4

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: f4 is the Vienna Gambit: it attacks e5 and opens the f-file.
notes.6: fxe5 gains space and pushes the f6 knight away.
notes.9: …Bg4 pins the knight and hopes to win time.
notes.10: Qe2 attacks the e4 knight a third time and frees White's game.

lines.summary: When Black pins with …Bg4, hit the e4 knight with Qe2.

lines.name: 3…exf4

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: f4 is the Vienna Gambit: it attacks e5 and opens the f-file.
notes.6: e5 kicks the knight back to g8, a big gain of time.
notes.10: d4 builds a strong centre and opens the bishop to win back f4.
notes.12: Qe2 pins the e5 pawn on the e-file, so White wins it back.

lines.summary: If Black takes the gambit pawn, kick the knight with e5 and build a big centre with d4.

lines.name: vs 2…Nc6 (3.Bc4)

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: Bc4 aims at f7; against 2…Nc6 it is safer than an early f4.
notes.6: d3 protects e4 so that f4 can come next.
notes.8: f4 attacks e5 and opens the f-file once White castles.

lines.summary: Against 2…Nc6, play Bc4 and d3 first, then the f4 push with Nf3 and castling.

lines.name: Na4 trades the bishop

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: Bc4 aims at f7; against 2…Nc6 it is safer than an early f4.
notes.6: d3 protects e4 so that f4 can come next.
notes.8: f4 attacks e5 and opens the f-file once White castles.
notes.12: Na4 trades off the c5 bishop, which stops White from castling safely.
notes.16: O-O and the f-file is ready for White's rook.

lines.summary: Trade off the dangerous c5 bishop with Na4, then castle and use the f-file.

lines.name: 4…Na5

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: Bc4 aims at f7; against 2…Nc6 it is safer than an early f4.
notes.6: d3 protects e4 so that f4 can come next.
notes.8: Nge2 keeps the f-pawn free and lets Black take the bishop.
notes.10: dxc4 recaptures towards the centre; White's pawns control d5.

lines.summary: If …Na5 chases the bishop, let it be taken and recapture with the d-pawn.

lines.name: vs 2…Bc5 (3.Bc4)

notes.2: Nc3 defends e4 and prepares f4, without blocking the f-pawn.
notes.4: Bc4 mirrors Black's bishop and keeps the plan simple.
notes.10: Nf3: this is the same position as the 2…Nc6 line.

lines.summary: 2…Bc5 reaches the same position as 2…Nc6: Bc4, d3, f4 and Nf3.
